note:
⛔ SNG-440. PHYSICAL RANGED CRAFT — Erik: 'I want more physical skills. Some can use agility, such as throwing knives, stars, stones. Some should be bow or crossbow style. Some are various raw power thrown.'
⚠️ MEASURED FIRST: of 376 abilities, only 45 are `physical` (12%, against 161 mental), and exactly ONE was a genuine ranged physical attack. 21 of 31 traditions have NO physical ability at all.
⛔ AUTHORED AS `valley_craft` ON PURPOSE. Valley craft is 'skill and nothing else' — no power system, no tradition gate — so these are available to ANY character and they close the coverage gap at the same time as the physical one. A Cogitant can now throw a knife. ⚠️ ALL SIX ROLL DICE on the existing ladder (L1 1d6, L2 2d6), because Erik's standard is that a skill DOES what its label says.

⛔ RE-ROOTED, SNG-443. ERIK: 'Skills may be learned at PLACES — or in the wilds as a hunter — but they would be TIED BACK TO THEIR TRADITION ROOTS otherwise.'
⚠️ THAT IS TWO AXES AND I HAD COLLAPSED THEM INTO ONE. `tradition` is the LINEAGE a craft descends from; `learnedAt` is where a person can actually acquire it. ⛔ FILING EVERYTHING AS valley_craft BECAUSE IT WAS OPEN TO ANYONE CONFUSED ACCESS WITH ANCESTRY.
⛔ AND IT DISSOLVES THE HUNTER'S STRIKE COLLISION RATHER THAN PATCHING IT: Hunter's Strike is a working hunter's shot, valley-rooted, learned in the wilds, taken for meat. The Drawn Bow is line-holding doctrine at range, marcher-rooted, learned at Hardline for money. ⚠️ SAME WEAPON, DIFFERENT CRAFT, DIFFERENT ROOT — they were never duplicates, they were two crafts I had mislabelled as one.

abilities.name: The Thrown Edge
abilities.narrationHints: The hand goes to the belt and comes away empty and there is already a knife in them. No draw, no aim you could see, no sound until it lands.
abilities.description: Put a knife, a star or a spike into someone at eight paces, underhand and without a windup. Quiet, deniable, and it does not announce itself the way a drawn bow does.
abilities.notFor: Armour without a gap; anything past a room's width; a fight you want witnessed.

tree.name: Underhand
tree.grants: One blade at 8 paces, from concealment or mid-stride. No windup a watcher could call.
tree.cannot: Cannot punch through mail or a shield; one blade per action.

tree.name: The Second Knife
tree.grants: Two blades in the time of one — the same target twice, or two targets standing close.
tree.cannot: Two targets must be standing close; you are still out of blades eventually.

tree.name: The Full Belt
tree.grants: Throw anything with a point and an edge, and it flies true: a chisel, a shard, a fork.
tree.cannot: Improvised points do less than a true blade; you must have something with an edge.

bounds.text: needs a blade or a point — improvised counts, empty hands do not
⛔ EIGHT PACES — past that the blade tumbles and lands flat
you must recover your knives afterward or you are out

abilities.plainly: A fight/stealth/duel action that deals damage. It rolls 1d6. Range is 8.
abilities._rootWhy: ⛔ THE EDGE, THROWN. A blade leaving the hand is still skill at arms, and the Marchers teach it even though they consider it a poor cousin of a held weapon. ⚠️ Learned at Hardline for money, or in the wilds by anyone who has had to eat.

abilities.name: The Sling and Stone
abilities.narrationHints: Two turns of the wrist and a sound like a wasp going past, and the man at the far end of the field sits down. The stone was free. There will be another one.
abilities.description: Whip a stone out to forty paces hard enough to drop a man, using ammunition that is lying on the ground everywhere you will ever stand.
abilities.notFor: Close quarters; silence; anything you need to hit through a shield.

tree.name: The Loosed Stone
tree.grants: One stone at 40 paces. Ammunition is whatever is underfoot — you are never out.
tree.cannot: Needs room to swing; useless in a press or a low tunnel.

tree.name: The Aimed Stone
tree.grants: Call the hit — a hand, a knee, the lamp, the horse. It goes where you called.
tree.cannot: Called shots at range still miss; loud in the way a bow is not.

tree.name: Skull-Weight
tree.grants: Lead or cast shot instead of river stone: it goes through a helm and keeps going.
tree.cannot: Cast shot must be carried and counted; still needs room to swing.

bounds.text: loud — everyone hears where it came from
one stone per action; you must find or carry them

abilities.plainly: A fight/survive/chase action that deals damage. It rolls 1d6. Range is 40.
abilities._rootWhy: ⛔ GENUINELY FOLK, AND ROOTED THERE. A shepherd's weapon: free ammunition, learned young, carried without anyone calling it a weapon. ⚠️ No tradition taught this; the valley did.

abilities.name: The Drawn Bow
abilities.narrationHints: You are not fast. You are UNHURRIED, which is different and much worse for them — the third arrow is already nocked while they are deciding whether to run at you or away.
abilities.description: Put an arrow through someone at a hundred and twenty paces, and keep doing it while they cross the ground between you.
abilities.notFor: Anything within arm's reach; fighting in a crowd; rain without a case.

tree.name: The Long Draw
tree.grants: One arrow at 120 paces, through leather and gambeson. You can hold at full draw and wait.
tree.cannot: Cannot shoot in a press; a shield-wall stops you cold; wet string, no shot.

tree.name: The Kept Rhythm
tree.grants: An arrow every action without losing accuracy — you can hold a corridor or a bridge alone.
tree.cannot: Arrows are counted — a quiver is twenty and you will notice.

tree.name: The Heavy Head
tree.grants: Bodkin heads: mail and plate stop mattering at under sixty paces.
tree.cannot: Bodkin heads only bite inside sixty paces; still both hands and clear sight.

bounds.text: ⛔ BOTH HANDS AND CLEAR SIGHT — no bow works in a grapple
arrows are counted; a quiver is twenty

abilities.plainly: A fight/survive/duel action that deals damage. It rolls 2d6. Range is 120.
abilities._rootWhy: ⛔ MILITARY ARCHERY. Holding a bridge alone, an arrow every action, the unhurried third shot — that is the March's line-holding doctrine at range and it descends from the Edge. ⚠️ DISTINCT FROM HUNTER'S STRIKE, which is a working hunter's shot for meat. Same weapon, different craft, different root.

abilities.name: The Levelled Crossbow
abilities.narrationHints: It does not care how strong you are or how long you trained. It is a machine that stores a stronger man's pull and gives it back on a hair trigger, and the bolt goes through a breastplate like the breastplate was a suggestion.
abilities.description: Level a crossbow and put a bolt through armour at ninety paces — and you can hand one to a farmer and they can do it too, which is the whole political problem with the thing.
abilities.notFor: Volume of fire; subtlety; anywhere carrying one gets you stopped at the gate.

tree.name: Spanned and Levelled
tree.grants: One bolt at 90 paces, through mail. Aim is trivial; anyone can be taught in an afternoon.
tree.cannot: ⛔ SPANNING TAKES A FULL ACTION — one shot, then you are a man holding a stick.

tree.name: The Belt Claw
tree.grants: Span and shoot in the same action, if you have both feet under you.
tree.cannot: You need both feet under you; a cranked string in the wet is a slow disaster.

tree.name: The Windlass
tree.grants: A heavy bow that will go through plate, a shield, and the arm behind it.
tree.cannot: Heavy, obvious, and illegal in three cities.

bounds.text: ⛔ RESPANNING COSTS AN ACTION at r1
heavy, obvious, and illegal in three cities
a cranked string in the wet is a slow disaster

abilities.plainly: A fight/duel/survive action that deals damage. It rolls 2d6. Range is 90.
abilities._rootWhy: ⚠️ MARCHER ROOT, BUT THE POLITICS ARE THE POINT: 'you can hand one to a farmer and they can do it too.' ⛔ The Marchers teach it and quietly resent that teaching is barely required. Illegal in three cities for exactly this reason.

abilities.name: The Hurled Weight
abilities.narrationHints: There is no craft in it and that is the craft. You get under the thing, you commit your whole body, and it goes. People do not expect the furniture.
abilities.description: Pick up something heavy and throw it hard enough to matter — a stone, a keg, a bench, a man. Fifteen paces, and what it hits stops being shaped the way it was.
abilities.notFor: Range; precision; anything delicate; a bare room.

tree.name: Get Under It
tree.grants: Throw anything you could lift at 15 paces. Objects break; people go down and stay down a moment.
tree.cannot: Needs something to throw and room to wind up; you are off balance afterward.

tree.name: The Committed Throw
tree.grants: Throw something you should not be able to lift — a table, a door, a person of your own size.
tree.cannot: You must be able to lift it; fifteen paces and it drops.

tree.name: The Scattering
tree.grants: Throw into a group: everyone in the path goes over, not just the first.
tree.cannot: One throw, one line — and recovering costs you an action.

bounds.text: ⛔ YOU MUST HAVE SOMETHING TO THROW and be able to lift it
you are off balance afterward — a full action to recover

abilities.plainly: A fight/survive action that deals damage. It rolls 1d6. Range is 15.
abilities._rootWhy: ⛔ SOMA. 'Get under it, commit your whole body' is the perfected-body discipline applied to a bench. ⚠️ Not the Edge — there is no weapon in it, only a person and something heavy.

abilities.name: The Quick Hands
abilities.narrationHints: Your hand is where the thing is going to be. Not fast exactly — EARLY, because you read the throw before it left the hand.
abilities.description: Catch, snatch or redirect a thing in flight — an arrow, a thrown blade, a dropped lamp, a purse leaving your belt — and have it in your hand instead of where it was going.
abilities.notFor: Crossbow bolts; anything heavy; things thrown from outside your sight.

tree.name: Early Hands
tree.grants: Catch or deflect one thrown object per action if you saw it thrown. Also: take a small thing off a person without them feeling it.
tree.cannot: You must SEE it coming — nothing from behind; one object per action.

tree.name: The Turned Catch
tree.grants: Catch it and send it back in the same motion, at the thrower, at short range.
tree.cannot: Short range only on the return; still nothing from behind.

tree.name: Both Hands
tree.grants: Two objects, or one arrow from a bow you did not see drawn.
tree.cannot: ⛔ NOT A BOLT — a crossbow bolt takes the hand off.

bounds.text: you must SEE it coming — nothing from behind
⛔ NOT A BOLT. A crossbow bolt takes the hand off
one object per action at r1

abilities.plainly: A fight/stealth/investigate action that catches or redirects something in flight. Its strength is rated 5 out of 10.
abilities._rootWhy: ⛔ PERFECT MOTION, NARROWED. Catching a thrown thing early is the Somatic reading-of-movement at hand scale. ⚠️ Also the pickpocket's craft, which the Flesh-Temples do not discuss.
abilities._perceiveReview: ⛔ SNG-455: perceive tag reviewed per rank. Kept where the player receives information they act on; stripped where the perceiving is the ability's internal mechanism.

_schemaFix: ⛔ SNG-452. Erik: 'make sure you're authoring with FULL SCHEMA CORRECTNESS.' ⚠️ ALL NINE ABILITIES I AUTHORED THIS SESSION WERE INCOMPLETE — the merged three missing axes/notFor/operativeAxis/bounds and every rank missing gains/harmRung; the six ranged missing cannot/functions/gains/harmRung on every rank. ⛔ I CHECKED THE CONTENT AND NOT THE SHAPE, which is the same failure as verifying content and not address.
